Furthermore, due to the war-like situation in West Asia and the Red Sea crisis,
our exports have completely collapsed, and shipping costs have skyrocketed
by 200% to 300%. Similarly, cotton, soybean, and maize farmers in Dhule and
Jalgaon are in deep distress as prices have fallen below the actual cost of
production. The grape growers of Nashik and the banana farmers of Jalgaon
are fighting a battle on two fronts: global conflict and climate change. The
unseasonal rain and hailstorms in January and February 2026 have already
damaged crops over more than 50,000 hectares of land.

decisive action. A guaranteed legal MSP must be provided for onions, and the
government should provide a 50% direct subsidy on transport to compensate
for the surge in freight costs caused by global tensions. Furthermore, the
number of NAFED and CCI procurement centers in Dhule and North
Maharashtra must be increased to ensure 100% procurement of cotton,
soybean, and maize at MSP. Additionally, a special financial package should
be announced for the farmers of North Maharashtra who have suffered heavy
losses due to these unseasonal rains and global market fluctuations.
Madam, if the Government does not intervene immediately, the rural
economy of North Maharashtra will be completely devastated. I earnestly
request the government, through this House, to rescue our Annadata from this
dire crisis and provide them with the justice they deserve.
Thank you.

downtrodden people are very much affected. Moreover, this is the season for

to give back immediately the seized money and material to those affected
people. Because they cannot approach Election Commission to get back their

patient who came to India from Myanmar, for dialysis was carrying money with
him and that money was seized on his way to a hospital. Election Commission
should immediately intervene in such matters and refund all those money to
those from whom it was collected. Following such a strict procedure adds to
the difficulties faced in today's world. Therefore, I urge that an Amendment be
brought in Election Code of Conduct or the Election related Laws which is the
need of the hour.

Tirunelveli Express, as much as Rs. 4 crore of unaccounted money was seized

Elections in Tamil Nadu. But it is still unclear that what has happened to that
seized money? He was Mr Nainar Nagendran the BJP candidate. It remains
unclear as to what happened to that huge money that was seized from such a
highly placed person. But the poor people are affected day in and day out.

Devendra Fadnavis—the Wainganga-Nalganga River Linking Project.

river, designed to provide water for agriculture, domestic use, and industrial
purposes. On March 9, 2026, this massive infrastructure project, valued at

initiative is truly historic: it involves the acquisition of 31,495 hectares of land,
will create a command area of 4.04 lakh hectares, and will ultimately provide
irrigation to over 6.11 lakh hectares.

of the law. But what we see today is not fairness. It is institutionalised
compromise at the cost of public wealth.
The Bill introduces definitions of avoidance transactions and fraudulent
trading. But definitions are not enforcement. Where is the accountability?
Where is the mechanism to ensure that those who syphon funds, mismanage
companies, and defraud creditors, are punished? They very well know the
names of the ones who have syphoned funds and escaped the country. But
what are they doing to bring them back? The Supreme Court in Swiss Ribbons
v. Union of India upheld the IBC precisely because it was designed to prevent
errant promoters from regaining control without paying their dues. But in
practise, what is the actual reality? They did not mention what is the actual
status and what is the reality right now. Promoters are walking away; banks
are taking losses; and the public has to pay.
The Bill does nothing to strengthen enforcement under Section 66. It
does nothing to ensure recovery from those who have caused the damage.
One of the most dangerous aspects of the Bill is excessive reliance on
delegated legislation. We have seen that in all the other Government Bills that
they bring into play. Especially in critical frameworks like group insolvency and
cross-border insolvency, which are not defined in the law itself, they fail to
mention that. Instead, they are left to rules and regulations. This is not reform.
This is complete abdication.
The Supreme Court in multiple judgments has clearly held that essential
legislative functions cannot be delegated. But the Government is

Security Fund financed through aggregator contributions;

workers in cities, such as Bengaluru, given the scale of the sector and the

age protection, etc. The Code provides for setting up of a Social Security Fund

The Government in its Budget announcement for financial year 2025-26
had announced several key measures for the welfare of Gig workers of online
platforms (platform workers) viz. their registration on the eShram portal,
issuance of identity cards, and extension of health care benefits under
Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY).
The Ministry of Labour and Employment had launched eShram portal on
26.08.2021 for creation of a comprehensive National Database of Unorganised
Workers including platform workers, migrant workers etc. The eShram portal is
meant to register and support the unorganised workers by providing them a
Universal Account Number (UAN) on a self-declaration basis. The Ministry of
Labour and Employment has also launched the eShram- ‘One-Stop-Solution’
that entails integration of different social security/welfare schemes at single
portal i.e., eShram portal. This is envisaged to enable unorganised workers
including platform workers registered on eShram to access social security
schemes including health care benefits under AB-PMJAY and see benefits
availed by them so far, through eShram portal.
The Ministry has also launched a dedicated Aggregator Module on
12.12.2024 for onboarding of aggregators on eShram portal. Till date, 21
aggregators including Zomato, Blinkit, Swiggy, Ola, Uber, Rapido, Amazon,
Porter, Urban Company, Flipkart etc. have onboarded on eShram portal. Also,
Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) have been developed on this
Module for verification and sharing details of platform workers engaged with
the aggregators.

placement- linked skill development and digital training access in tribal
districts like Nandurbar?

been implementing its flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana
(PMKVY), since 2015, for imparting skill development training through Short-
Term Training (STT) and up-skilling and re-skilling through Recognition of Prior
Learning (RPL), to all sections of the society across the country, including in
tribal and aspirational districts. The Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) serves as an
integrated digital platform providing access to skill courses, career guidance,
apprenticeship opportunities and other skilling-related services. These
initiatives are implemented across all States/UTs, including Maharashtra and
its tribal districts such as Nandurbar.
PMKVY 4.0 is a demand driven Scheme and skill training centres are
accredited and affiliated based on the requirements received from State/
industry/ industry associations/ training providers.
MSDE conducts periodic independent evaluations of PMKVY to ensure
quality and accountability. An evaluation by NITI Aayog (October 2020)
indicated that approximately 94 percent of surveyed employers expressed
willingness to hire more candidates trained under PMKVY. The study also
noted that 52 percent of candidates placed in employment or oriented under
the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) component reported receiving higher
salaries or expecting improved earnings compared to uncertified peers. An

independent evaluation of PMKVY 2.0 conducted by the Indian Institute of

candidates were placed in their desired skill sector.
More recently, an independent third-party impact evaluation of the
PMKVY 4.0 has been conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial
Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous institution of Ministry of Finance,
Government of India, across the country including the State of Maharashtra.
The Study also covered aspirational and tribal districts. As per the report,
PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift in employment
outcomes for STT candidates. The combined share of employed and self-
employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4%
after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income-
related outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates
and 48.9% of RPL candidates reporting an increase in income following
training and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded
access to formal skill training and certification and has generated measurable
improvements in skill confidence, employment participation, and income
outcomes for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries.

industries, business associations, and private sector employers. These

organizing industry consultations to gain deeper insights into sector-specific

the placements opportunities to the certified candidates.

development and entrepreneurship among Scheduled Tribe communities.

culture, heritage, spirituality, wellness, yoga, adventure, wildlife, cuisine, luxury

THE MINISTER OF FINANCE; AND MINISTER OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS
(SHRIMATI NIRMALA SITHARAMAN):
(a): The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) consolidates the laws
relating to reorganisation and insolvency resolution of corporate persons,
partnership firms and individuals in a time bound manner for maximisation of
value of assets of such persons. The IBC has established four pillars of
insolvency namely the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India, defined the
Adjudicating Authority, Information Utility and the Insolvency Professionals.
(b): In the pre-IBC period, there was no single law that dealt with insolvency
and bankruptcy. The Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985,
the Recovery of Debt Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993, the
Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of
Security Interest Act, 2002 and the Companies Act, 2013 had provisions
relating to insolvency and bankruptcy. The IBC has consolidated all these
fragmented laws and resolved 1419 companies as on 31st March 2026. These
cases have led to a recovery of ₹ 4.32 lakh crore to the creditors, which
amounts to a realisation of 94.6% of fair value and 166.9% of liquidation value.
IBC has enhanced the ease of doing business by providing a time-bound and
transparent mechanism for resolving insolvency, improving investor
confidence and credit availability.

Performing Assets (GNPA) ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks has declined
from its peak of 11.2% in March 2018 to a low of 1.8% in March 2026.
The impact of the IBC on credit discipline has also been corroborated by
a comprehensive study conducted by the Indian Institute of Management
Bangalore (IIMB). The study finds that IBC has prompted borrowers to adhere
to stipulated loan payment schedules. During the period under review, the
study notes a significant reduction in loan accounts deemed ‘Overdue’, both in
terms of the Rupee amount as well as in terms of the number of accounts.

(August 2023; available at www.ibbi.gov.in), analysed the financial
performance of firms that underwent resolution under the IBC and found
significant improvements in the profitability, liquidity, and overall financial
health of resolved firms in the post-resolution period. These findings
underscore the positive impact of IBC on business continuity and value
preservation.

from its peak of 11.2% in March 2018 to a low of 1.8% in March 2026.

a comprehensive study conducted by the Indian Institute of Management
Bangalore (IIMB). The study finds that IBC has prompted borrowers to adhere
to stipulated loan payment schedules. During the period under review, the
study notes a significant reduction in loan accounts deemed ‘Overdue’, both in
terms of the Rupee amount as well as in terms of the number of accounts.
A report by the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIM-A)
(August 2023; available at www.ibbi.gov.in), analysed the financial
performance of firms that underwent resolution under the IBC and found
significant improvements in the profitability, liquidity, and overall financial
health of resolved firms in the post-resolution period. These findings
underscore the positive impact of IBC on business continuity and value
preservation.

sponsored schemes namely, Samagra Shiksha, PM Schools for Rising India
(PM SHRI), Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) and
Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society (ULLAS) have been aligned
with the objectives and vision of NEP 2020.
NEP 2020 gives the highest priority to achieving universal Foundational
Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) for all children by Grade 2 and accordingly, the
Department launched National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with
Understanding and Numeracy (NIPUN Bharat Mission) under the aegis of the
NEP and aligned with centrally sponsored scheme of Samagra Shiksha for
early learning across States and Union Territories.
Implemented across the country, a range of interventions have been
undertaken under the Mission. These include nationwide implementation of
Vidya Pravesh, a three-month school-readiness module for all Grade 1
students; large-scale teacher and school head training through NISHTHA
(National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement)-
FLN focusing on activity-based and child-centric pedagogy; provision of play-
based and digital learning resources such as DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for
Knowledge Sharing)- FLN content, Jaadui Pitara- a collection of Learning
Teaching Material (LTM) & e-Jaadui Pitara for children in the 3–8 age group,
Primers developed in 121 Local Languages for foundational literacy and
numeracy in mother tongue and teaching learning material for students.
Further, guidelines on co-location of Anganwadi Centres with primary
schools, released on 3rd September 2025, ensure convergence between

NEP 2020 provides for 50 hours of Continuous Professional

National Mission for Mentoring (NMM) was launched for creation of a large
pool of outstanding professionals willing to provide mentoring to school
teachers.

the approach of “Anyone, Anywhere, Anytime” Learning. There have been

distribution of SWAYAM Enrolments is given in the enclosed Statement-III.

of 1,12,822 video contents, equivalent to 32,763 hours of telecast has been
produced by States/UTs and Autonomous Bodies in 45 languages, thereby
facilitating equitable and inclusive access to quality education.

including NISHTHA and other departmental training programmes. Students

curriculum-based educational content is disseminated through the five PM

(e) whether the Government has any data of the total compensation disbursed
in Telangana for human deaths, injuries, livestock loss and crop damage, if
so, the details thereof, category-wise and if not, the reasons for lack of
consolidated data?
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE
(SHRI BHUPENDER YADAV):
(a): The management of wildlife including mitigation of human-animal
conflicts is primarily the responsibility of the concerned State
Government/Union Territory Administration. The State Government/UT
Administration are the first responders to any conflict situation and they
maintain the details of the conflict along with the species involved. Under the
Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats
an amount of Rs. 323.32 lakhs, Rs. 291.68 lakhs, Rs. 302.34 lakhs and Rs.
208.67 lakhs have been released to the State of Telangana during the
financial years 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 & 2026-27 respectively for inter
alia management of Human wildlife conflict.
(b) to (e): Under the said scheme, activities supported include procurement
of early warning systems, construction and erection of physical barriers such
as solar powered electric fencing, bio-fencing, trenches, boundary walls etc.
to prevent depredation by wild animals which inter alia includes cattle lifting,
crop damage, loss of life and property. Rapid Response Teams with
community stewards are also deployed to mitigate Human-Wildlife Conflict.

The Government of India has assessed the status of human wildlife
conflict across the country including Telangana especially in context of
flagship species such as tigers and elephants wherein during the last
decade no human deaths due to elephants and only 3 human deaths due to
tiger attacks were reported by the State of Telangana. Further, granular data
in respect of compensation and affected districts is collated at level of the
State.
Important steps taken by the Government to manage human-wildlife
conflicts include the following:
i. Section 11 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 adequately
empowers the State Chief Wild Life Wardens to manage wildlife in
conflict situations.
ii. The Ministry has issued advisories and guidelines to manage human-
wildlife negative interactions through interdepartmental coordinated
actions besides adherence to SOPs in this regard. Use of
technological aids are used to strengthen these interventions.
iii. The Ministry has established a Centre of Excellence for Human–
Wildlife Conflict Management at the Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology
and Natural History (SACON), WII–South India Centre, Coimbatore, to
strengthen the scientific and institutional framework for managing
human–wildlife conflict.

The scheme aims to incentivise creation of more than 3.5 Crore jobs all
across the country, over a period of 2 years including the state of
Maharashtra. The scheme comprises of two parts i.e. Part A and Part B and
focuses on providing support to both employees and employers by way of
incentives. The scheme provides for incentives for 1.92 crore eligible First
time employees under Part A. Incentive for creation of approximately 2.59
crore additional jobs to employers is provided for under Part B of the scheme.
The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is the implementing
agency for the scheme.
Prime Minister disbursed incentives worth around ₹2,400 crore under
the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY) at a special
programme held on 19 June 2026 at New Delhi. As part of the nationwide
outreach effort, PM-VBRY events were also organised simultaneously at
around 200 locations across the country.
The PMVBRY is a demand-driven scheme. For the State of
Maharashtra, including Mumbai, under part A, incentive amount of Rs 149.41
crore has disbursed to 2.49 lakh first timer employees; and under Part B,
incentive amount of Rs 435.92 cr has been disbursed to 12,701 beneficiary
establishments.
The scheme and its provisions have been widely disseminated through
extensive outreach efforts across the country. EPFO has undertaken
awareness and stakeholder outreach programmes, including monthly Nidhi
Aapke Nikat (NAN) programmes, SMS/email and digital communication

research, infrastructure, governance and institutional best practices, and
awards accreditation grades based on their performance. The accreditation
process promotes quality assurance, accountability, research and innovation,
and serves as an important benchmark for institutional excellence and
continuous improvement in higher education.
To boost research and innovation, the Government has established the
Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), which seeks to harness
the research potential of universities and colleges, support academic research,
and facilitate translational research in emerging technologies and national
priority areas. The ANRF aims to mobilize ₹50,000 crore during 2023–28,
including ₹14,000 crore from the Central Government, with the remaining
sourced from public sector enterprises, the private sector, philanthropies, and
international bodies, through various funds such as the ANRF Fund, Innovation
Fund, and Science and Engineering Research Fund.
Other initiatives such as the Prime Minister's Research Fellowship
(PMRF), Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration
(SPARC), IMPRINT, Uchhatar Avishkar Yojana (UAY) and Institutions of
Eminence (IoE) continue to enhance research capacity, innovation and
collaboration between academia, industry and international institutions.
Focus of NEP on research and innovation has propelled India’s ranking
in the Global Innovation Index (GII) from 48 in 2020 and currently being ranked
at 38th place in 2025.

the research potential of universities and colleges, support academic research,
and facilitate translational research in emerging technologies and national
priority areas. The ANRF aims to mobilize ₹50,000 crore during 2023–28,
including ₹14,000 crore from the Central Government, with the remaining
sourced from public sector enterprises, the private sector, philanthropies, and
international bodies, through various funds such as the ANRF Fund, Innovation
Fund, and Science and Engineering Research Fund.
Other initiatives such as the Prime Minister's Research Fellowship
(PMRF), Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration
(SPARC), IMPRINT, Uchhatar Avishkar Yojana (UAY) and Institutions of
Eminence (IoE) continue to enhance research capacity, innovation and
collaboration between academia, industry and international institutions.
Focus of NEP on research and innovation has propelled India’s ranking
in the Global Innovation Index (GII) from 48 in 2020 and currently being ranked
at 38th place in 2025.

in India, including SC, ST, OBC and minority students get scholarships as per
Scheme guidelines.

new central sector scheme in November 2024 to facilitate access to collateral-
free and guarantor-free education loans for meritorious students pursuing
higher education.

Ministry of Tribal Affairs is also implementing two Central Sector
Schemes- National Fellowship for Higher Education for ST students and
National Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students (Top Class).
Further, National Overseas Scholarship for ST students is implemented
through the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and the funds are released to ST
students studying abroad through Embassies. Ministry of Tribal Affairs further
reimburse the funds to MEA.
For promotion of internationalisation of education, the Government has
enabled the setting up of Foreign Higher Educational Institutions (FHEIs) in
India. 16 Letters of Intent have been issued to FHEIs from Australia, Italy,
United Kingdom and USA to set up their campuses at various places in India.
Among these, University of Southampton, UK commenced its courses in
August, 2025 at its campus in Gurugram, Haryana. Under International
Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) Regulations 2022, approvals
have been accorded to 5 universities from UK, Australia and Northern Ireland
for operating offshore branch campuses in GIFT City SEZ, Gandhinagar,
Gujarat. Among these 5 universities, Deakin University, Australia commenced
its courses in July, 2024, and University of Wollongong, Australia commenced
its courses in November, 2024. In addition, Indian institutions are also
establishing a global presence, with IIT Delhi’s campus in Abu Dhabi, IIM
Ahmedabad campus in Dubai and IIT Madras in Tanzania. These steps
support the goal of making India a global hub for education.

THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI
GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT):
(a) and (b): Ministry of Tourism under its Scheme “Pilgrimage Rejuvenation
and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive” (PRASHAD) provides financial
assistance to the State Governments (SGs) and Union Territory
Administrations (UTAs) for development of tourism related infrastructure at
identified religious and heritage sites across the country including the State of
Tamil Nadu. The details of the total funds sanctioned, released and utilized
under the said scheme, State/UT wise including Tamil Nadu are given in the
enclosed Statement.
(c): The development of tourism infrastructure and visitor amenities under the
PRASHAD scheme is intended to facilitate improved accessibility, better visitor
experience and the overall development of pilgrimage destinations.

8. SUSHRI KANGNA RANAUT:
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has assessed the long-term outcomes of

and community engagement;

higher education or took up leadership roles thereafter;

providing them opportunities for personality development, skill enhancement,
community engagement and exposure to public service. MY Bharat (erstwhile
NYKS) implements various youth development and community service
programmes across the country, including Himachal Pradesh.
The Ministry periodically reviews the implementation of the Scheme
through reports submitted by MY Bharat, review meetings and monitoring

Working Conditions (OSH&WC) Code, 2020 with effect from 21st November,

(c) and (d): The Labour Codes were enacted to meet need for comprehensive

integration, strengthen social Security and ensure workplace safety and

mandatory issue of appointment letter, universalisation of social security by

strengthen their protection against employment-related vulnerabilities and
enabling greater adaptability to new forms of work like gig & platform work and
technology-driven employment models.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PANKAJ
CHOUDHARY):
(a) : Since 2020-21, Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, Government
of India is implementing scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital
Investment (SASCI). Under the scheme, 50-year interest free loan is provided to
the state Governments for capital projects. Since 2025-26, Union Territories with
Legislature are also provided assistance under SASCI. The objective of the
scheme to assist the States/UT Administrations in boosting capital expenditure
and to promote reforms in key areas.
Yes, the scheme includes reform linked components. In 2026-27, SASCI
includes 12 parts including Part I (untied), Part II (State/UT Share of Centrally
Sponsored Schemes and Central Projects) and following reform-based parts:
i. Part III: Incentives for Achieving Targets for Capital Expenditure
ii. Part IV: Strengthening Public Finance IT Infrastructure in States
iii. Part V: Mining Sector Reforms
iv. Part VI: Implementation of the Right of Way Rules, 2024 under the
Telecommunications Act, 2023
v. Part VII: Digital Public Infrastructure for Agriculture – AgriStack
vi. Part VIII: Livestock Sector Reforms
vii. Part IX: Efficiency in Financial Management

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PANKAJ

(a): Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has apprised that strengthening of corporate
governance frameworks in banks is an ongoing exercise undertaken by RBI to
ensure a robust, transparent and efficient banking system aligned with global best
practices.
In the recent past, RBI has issued instructions pertaining to independence
of Board and Board Committees, quorum requirements, requirement for a bank
Chairperson to be an Independent Director, age and tenure limits, fit and proper
criteria, succession planning, remuneration etc., in respect of Non-executive
Directors (NEDs) as well as Whole-time Directors (WTDs), etc.
(b): In terms of the guidelines issued by RBI on ‘On-tap’ licensing of Universal
Banks and Small Finance Banks in the Private Sector, dated 28.11.2025, existing
NBFCs are permitted to apply to the Reserve Bank for promoting or conversion to
Universal Bank and Small Finance Bank.
(c): As regards RRBs, the existing instructions on Governance, Board procedures,
Committees of the Board etc. have been consolidated and issued as ‘RBI (RRBs-
Governance) Directions’ on 28.11.2025. For better governance, Government has
appointed Government Nominee Directors in the board of all RRBs. Further,

the Observatory of Economic Complexity (OEC), India's ranking on the Economic

More recently, an independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY
4.0 has been conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial
Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous institution of Ministry of Finance,
Government of India, across the country including the State of Maharashtra. As
per the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift in
employment outcomes for STT candidates. The combined share of employed and
self-employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4%
after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income-
related outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates
and 48.9% of RPL candidates reporting an increase in income following training
and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded access to formal
skill training and certification and has generated measurable improvements in skill
confidence, employment participation, and income outcomes for a substantial
proportion of beneficiaries.

honorarium, TA/DA, boarding and lodging, local transport etc. which help
supplement their income and encourage them to pursue their art as a sustainable
livelihood, thereby contributing to their self-reliance.

Progress of implementation of action plans is reviewed by the RRC’s at
State Level and by Central Monitoring Committee (CMC) constituted under the
Chairmanship of Secretary, Ministry of Jal Shakti at Central Level.
Under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), four Non-attainment
cities in Karnataka have been covered for implementation of air quality
improvement measures. These cities namely Bengaluru, Davanagere, Kalaburagi
(Gulbarga) and Hubballi-Dharwad were provided air quality performance based
incentive grant of ₹ 625.94 crore during FY 2019-20 till 2025-26 for undertaking
various air pollution mitigation measures as per the City action plans.
All four NCAP cities in the State have shown improvement in average
PM₁₀ concentration during 2025-26 as compared to the base year 2017-18.
Davanagere and Kalaburagi (Gulbarga) have achieved compliance with the
National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for PM₁₀. Davanagere
recorded the highest improvement of 41%, followed by Hubballi-Dharwad with
23%, and Bengaluru with 17% improvement.
Further, the city-wise air quality status of Karnataka cities covered under
the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) is given in the enclosed Statement-I.
The details of ambient air quality monitoring stations located in the State of
Karnataka are given in the enclosed Statement-II.

For the first time the definition of 'gig workers and 'platform workers and
provisions related to the same have been provided in the Code on Social
Security, 2020 which has come into force on 21.11.2025.
The Code provides for framing of suitable social security measures for gig
workers and platform workers on matters relating to life and disability cover,
accident insurance, health and maternity benefits, old age protection, etc. The
Code provides for setting up of a Social Security Fund to finance these welfare
schemes for which one of the sources is contribution from aggregators between 1
to 2% of annual turnover of an aggregator subject to the limit of 5% of the amount
paid or payable by an aggregator to such workers. The Code also has provisions
to constitute a National Social Security Board for the purposes of the welfare of
gig workers and platform workers.

platform workers. The Rules operationalize the provisions of the Code by

Areas' (A sub-scheme of Swadesh Darshan Scheme) under Pradhan Mantri
Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM-JUGA). The objective of the initiative is to
develop homestays in tribal areas to promote responsible tourism and enhance
livelihood opportunities for tribal communities. The guidelines also focus on
technical upskilling and training of the Homestay owners. The said initiative
includes development of 1000 homestays with support of Up to ₹5 lakh for village
community requirement, Up to ₹5 lakh for construction of two new rooms for each
household and Up to ₹3 lakh for renovation of existing rooms for each household.

various initiatives. As part of on-going activities; promotion of Rural homestays
and Rural Tourism is also taken up. In order to provide impetus for development
of Green and Eco Tourism in the country, Ministry of Tourism formulated National
Strategies for Eco Tourism and Sustainable Tourism and initiated Travel for LiFE

AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS (SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA):
(a) to (e): The legal framework for Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is
established under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, along with Schedule
VII of the Act and the Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, 2014. The items enlisted in
the Schedule VII are broad-based and intended to cover a wide range of
activities. Under the Companies Act, CSR is a Board driven process and the
Board of the company is empowered to plan, decide, execute and monitor CSR
activities of the company based on the recommendation of its CSR Committee.

enabling youth of India to get future ready, equipped with industry relevant skills.

During FY 2025-26, 14 complaints pertaining to 'Cash not available for long
time' under the category 'ATM/CDM/Debit card' were received at the Offices of the
RBI Ombudsman from the complainants in the state of 'Maharashtra'.
The Bank-wise and District- wise instances of cash out at an ATM for more
than 10 hours in a month reported for the period December 2025 to May 2026 is
given in the enclosed Statement.
Further, regarding accountability, there is a penalty framework put in place
by RBI to penalise banks for instances of cash out at an ATM for more than 10
hours in a month.
RBI has informed that it engages with banks regularly for their cash
requirements in the State and arranges for the same, as required, through supply
from Minting Presses and/or arrangement of cash from other Currency Chests. Its
Offices proactively monitor the stock at Currency Chests of the banks and supply
currency to banks for their cash requirements, and it engages periodically with
banks and other stakeholders involved in the ecosystem to identify and act on the
challenges identified in currency management and holds periodic meetings with
banks advising them to ensure adequate cash availability in ATMs.

framework for the environmentally sound collection, transportation, refurbishment

recyclers and bulk consumers. The Rules mandate registration of all stakeholders

mechanism, require manufacturers to ensure utilisation of recycled non-ferrous
metals, provide for generation and trading of EPR certificates by registered
recyclers, and require maintenance of records and filing of returns to facilitate
digital tracking, monitoring and enforcement of compliance.

Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs), a centrally sponsored
scheme with an investment of Rs.60,000 crore. The scheme envisages the
upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs across the country in a hub-and-spoke
model comprising 200 hub ITIs and 800 spoke ITIs. PM-SETU focuses on
improving employability outcomes through industry-led governance, and
indirectly supports self-employment and entrepreneurship by enabling
learners (including early-stage enterprises and first-time entrepreneurs) to
acquire industry-relevant skills, gain exposure to real work environments, and
access career guidance, placement support, and self-employment support
through strengthened institutional systems and industry linkages.

Committee. The Board of the company is required to disclose the CSR Policy

the person responsible for financial management shall certify to the effect. In

designated fund(s) in Schedule VII in the prescribed time limit. Further, the first
proviso to Section 135 (5) of the Act provides that the company shall give
preference to the local area and areas around it where it operates. However, the
emphasis on local area is only directory and not mandatory in nature and
companies need to balance local area preference with national priorities.

formulation of CSR policy, Annual Action Plan on CSR, identification of the
project and area in which project will be implemented, certification of CSR
expenditure by Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and audit of CSR expenditure by
statutory auditors, etc., provide adequate mechanisms to ensure transparency
and accountability.
Whenever any violation of CSR provisions is reported, action against such
non-compliant Companies is initiated as per provisions of the Companies Act,
2013 and rules made thereunder after due examination of records and following
due process of law.

TOURISM DEVELOPMENT UNDER SDS-2.0 IN SHAHDOL
56. SHRIMATI HIMADRI SINGH:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:
(a) the current status of tourist destinations or circuits identified in the Shahdol
Lok Sabha Constituency including Shahdol, Anuppur, and Umaria districts
under the Swadesh Darshan-2.0 scheme (SDS-2.0);
(b) the details of funds sanctioned, released, and utilized for upgrading tourism
infrastructure and last-mile connectivity at key regional sites like
Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve and Amarkantak during the last three years;
and
(c) the details of the specific steps taken by the Government under the said
scheme to promote sustainable tribal eco-tourism and generate local
employment for youth in the said constituency?
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI
GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT):
(a) to (c): Development and promotion of tourism destinations and products is
primarily undertaken by the concerned State Government (SG)/Union Territory
Administration (UTA). However, the Ministry of Tourism through its central sector
schemes of ‘Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0)’, ‘Challenge Based Destination
Development (CBDD)’, a sub-scheme of Swadesh Darshan scheme and
‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’

(b): CBDT has taken a series of technical and structural remediation measures to
further strengthen the infrastructure of the e-Filing portal ahead of the peak filing
period, including the following:
(i) The e-Filing ecosystem has been comprehensively strengthened and
performance-tested to support peak filing volumes, with validated capacity to
handle up to 1 crore ITRs per day, ensuring sufficient headroom beyond the
projected peak demand.

memory, network, and bandwidth. Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM)-
recommended hardware and software upgrades, along with storage
augmentation, have been implemented to improve overall system stability,
resilience, and input/output performance.
(iii) Major infrastructure issues identified during the earlier ITR filing seasons
have been rectified.
(iv) A robust monitoring and governance framework has been established, inter
alia, comprising 24×7 infrastructure monitoring, a dedicated WarRoom, and
coordinated participation of application, infrastructure, database, network,
security, vendor, and stakeholder teams to enable proactive monitoring and
rapid incident resolution.

Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development (NIESBUD) and the Indian
Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE) under the aegis of MSDE conduct

Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) nationwide to foster an
entrepreneurial mindset focus on training, credit access, and market access. PM
Vishwakarma scheme, launched in September 2023, provides holistic support
(upskilling, toolkits, and collateral-free credit) to artisans in 18 traditional trades.
MSDE launched Swavalambini programme in February 2025 in the North Eastern
States of Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and in Uttar Pradesh and Telangana to
cultivate entrepreneurial mindsets among female candidates. Thus far, total of
1200 female candidates have been trained under EAP and 602 candidates have
been trained under EDP.

Following welfare measures have been stipulated for workers under VB G
RAM G at worksite, as elaborated in Schedule II of VB G RAM G, 2025: -
i. The facilities of safe drinking water, shade for children and periods of rest,
first aid box with adequate material for emergency treatment for minor injuries
and other health hazards connected with the work being performed shall be
provided at the works site.
ii. In case the number of children below the age of five years accompanying the
women working at any site is five or more, provision shall be made to depute
one of such women workers to look after such children. The person so
deputed shall be paid wage rate.
iii. If any personal injury is caused to any person employed under the Scheme by
any accident arising out of and in the course of his employment, he shall be
entitled to such medical treatment as required, free of cost.
iv. Where hospitalisation of the injured worker is necessary, the State
Government shall arrange for such hospitalisation including accommodation,
treatment, medicines and payment of daily allowance which is not less than
half of the wage rate.
v. If a person employed under the Scheme meets with death or becomes
permanently disabled by accident arising out of and in the course of
employment, he or his legal heirs, as the case may be, shall be paid by the
implementing agency an ex gratia as per entitlements under the Pradhan

verification mechanisms;
(b) whether it is a fact that most recoveries rely on foreign law enforcement
rather than domestic efforts, if so, the details of India-led initiatives and if not,
the reasons for limited independent action;

Survey of India (ASI) capacity for tracking stolen artefacts globally, if so, the
budgetary and operational details thereof and if not, the reasons for
institutional under-preparedness;

created and regularly updated and if so, the access details thereof and if not,
the reasons for absence of transparent digital tracking systems; and
(e) whether the Government has taken steps to prevent ongoing smuggling of
temple idols and artefacts and if so, the enforcement measures thereof and if
not, the reasons for continued illicit trafficking networks?

THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI
GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT):
(a): A total of 655 antiquities have been repatriated and authenticated since 2014
to June 30, 2026.
(b) and (c): Government of India with the help of law-enforcement agencies takes-
up the repatriation process as per provisions of the Antiquities and Art Treasures
Act 1972 and the international Conventions and Practices. Further, the staff and
officers of the Archaeological Survey of India participate in the various training
sessions, seminars and workshops organised from time to time for the purpose of
dealing with matters to stop the illicit trafficking of antiquities.
(d): A database in respect of the theft from Monuments of National Importance,
Sites and the museums is available on the website of Archaeological Survey of
India https://asi.nic.in.
(e): The government takes necessary steps towards prevention of the theft of
antiquities. Besides regular watch and ward staff, private security guards and
Central Industrial Security Force have been deployed as per requirement at
Monuments of National Importance, Sites and Museums. Whenever any theft of
antiquity is reported; FIR is lodged and ‘Look out Notice’ is issued to the law-
enforcement agencies including Custom Exit Channels to keep vigil to trace
stolen antiquity and prevent export.

NAPS across more than 45 sectors. Major sectors include Automotive, IT-ITeS,
Electronics, Retail, Production & Manufacturing, Logistics, Telecom, Food
Processing, Agriculture, Apparel, Construction, Healthcare, Life Sciences and
Tourism & Hospitality. The sector-wise distribution of apprentices engaged under
NAPS is given in the enclosed Statement-II.
Further, trades relevant to the coastal economy are covered under NAPS
through various sectors such as Agriculture, Food Processing, Logistics and
Marine. These include trades such as Aquaculture Worker, Fish and Seafood
Processing Technician, Fish and Seafood Junior Processor, Pipe Fitter (Marine),
Rigger (Marine), Shipwright (Steel), Shipwright (Wood), Crane Operator-Port
Terminals/Container Freight Station (CFS) /Inland Container Depot(ICD), Junior
Cargo Operator-Port Terminals/CFS/ICD, Port Terminals/CFS/ICD Supervisor,
Bulk Cargo Inspector, International Freight Forwarding Executive, Cold Chain
Specialist, Warehouse Operations and other logistics-related trades.
Apprenticeship opportunities in these trades are available based on industry
demand and participation by establishments engaged in the respective sectors.
(d): The Apprentices Act, 1961 provides a framework for establishments to utilize
their training infrastructure and workplace facilities for imparting apprenticeship
training. Under the Act, establishments employing four or more workers are
eligible to engage apprentices, while engagement of apprentices is mandatory for
establishments having thirty or more workers, subject to the provisions of the Act.

Government has been organizing Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas

administrative considerations. Apprenticeship opportunities under NAPS are

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):
(a): The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) is a self-financed
autonomous body functioning under the aegis of the Department of School
Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, Government of India. CBSE does
not implement centrally sponsored education schemes such as Samagra Shiksha
Abhiyan, PM SHRI and PM POSHAN. Further, CBSE does not receive any funds
from Consolidated Fund of India.
However, the CBSE is liable to answer queries of Parliament Standing
Committee.
(b): No proposal in this regard has been moved by Ministry of Education.

86. SHRI RAO RAJENDRA SINGH:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) the number of vacancies in the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) as of
January 2026;
(b) the steps being taken by the Government to fill these posts and strengthen
direct tax administration capacity; and
(c) whether such large-scale vacancies have affected the efficiency of tax
collection and enforcement, especially in view of the increasing share of
cesses and surcharges in total direct tax revenue, if so, the details thereof?

regularly in the terms of mode of recruitment prescribed in the relevant
recruitment rules, namely direct recruitment through UPSC/SSC or through

support the scholars pursuing Ph.D. Special fellowships are provided for
Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, Persons with
Disabilities and Single Girl Child. The Ph.D. scholars are eligible to join research

funding to support their research, leading to the award of a Ph.D.

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):
(a) and (b): Under Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill Development
and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through
an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes, viz.
Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS),
National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training
Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of
the society across the country, including women in rural areas. SIM aims at
enabling youth of India to get future ready and equipped with industry relevant
skills.
The schemes of MSDE are demand driven and training centres under
these schemes are set up or engaged on need basis. State-wise details of the
number of training centres, including those in the Arani Lok Sabha Constituency
(Tiruvannamalai and Viluppuram districts) of Tamil Nadu, engaged under the
schemes of MSDE are given in the enclosed Statement- I. Year-wise detail of
the candidates trained/certified under various schemes of MSDE is given in the
enclosed Statement- II.

for mobile banking and Aadhaar-based financial services in inaccessible
regions?

(a) to (d): To ensure accessibility of banking services in rural and remote areas,
the endeavor of the Government is to provide a banking outlet [Bank branch /

kilometres of all inhabited villages in the country. Availability of banking outlets is
monitored by a Geographic Information System (GIS) based App., namely, Jan
Dhan Darshak (JDD) App.
As per the JDD app, 91% of the inhabited villages in the Union Territory
(UT) of Ladakh are covered by a banking outlet. Details of the banking
infrastructure in the UT of Ladakh are as under:

Commercial Banks (except Regional Rural Banks) to open bank branches
anywhere in India without prior approval, provided 25% are in unbanked rural
areas. In pursuance of extant RBI guidelines, rolling out of banking outlets in
uncovered areas is a continuous process looked after by the State Level
Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) / Union Territory Level Bankers Committee

coastal erosion and tidal ingress by Casuarina plantations.

climate adaptation project by the Green Climate Fund to tackle the twin issues
of sustainable development and climate resilience in coastal areas.

predation and pests, monospecific plantations, soil degradation, displacement of

during suitable planting seasons.

respective State Governments. However, DGT has supported the upgradation of

developed and approved by National Council for Vocational Education and
Training (NCVET). Additionally, 40 CTS courses have been revised and
approved to further align training with industry requirements. The list is attached
at enclosed Statement-II.

Initiatives for enhancing employability, workforce readiness,
apprenticeship opportunities and skill upgradation: In order to meet
skilling requirement for future workforce, improve the quality of skilling, to align
the training programs to market needs and improve the employability of
trainees, some of the steps taken by the Government include:
i. The training programs offered under the schemes of the Ministry are
developed in collaboration with industries, keeping in view the market
demands.
ii. Courses aligned to National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF) also
have components of On Job Training (OJT) and employability skills.
iii. The National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET)
has been set up as an overarching regulator establishing regulations
and standards to ensure quality in the Technical and Vocational
Education and Training (TVET) space. The Awarding Bodies
recognized by NCVET are required to develop the qualifications as per
the industry demand and obtain industry validations.
iv. Future ready job-roles addressing the requirement of Industry 4.0,
emerging sectors like Drone, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Robotics,
Mechatronics, etc., have been prioritized under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal
Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0.

NATIONAL AUDIT ON GOVERNMENT SCHOOLS
132. SHRI RAMASAHAYAM RAGHURAM REDDY:
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether any national audit has been conducted recently on the quality of
teaching and infrastructure in Government schools;
(b) if so, the proportion of schools without functional toilets, internet access,
or science labs, State/UT-wise;
(c) whether the Government is considering a minimum per-student
infrastructure budget if so, the details thereof States/UT-wise;
(d) whether implementation of National Education Policy (NEP) has resulted
in improved student learning outcomes; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):
(a): The quality of school education and infrastructure is monitored, audited
and assessed through various institutional mechanisms, including the
Performance Grading Index (PGI), UDISE+, PARAKH assessments, PM SHRI
School Quality Monitoring Framework, social audit and periodic review and
monitoring under the Samagra Shiksha Scheme. Further, States/UTs
undertake monitoring and evaluation of schools as per their respective
administrative arrangements.

performance under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 in development
of competencies and learning outcomes among students at the end of the
Foundational, Preparatory and Middle Stages (assessed in Grades 3, 6 and 9,
respectively) of education. This Sarvekshan is designed as a system-level
reflection on Learning Outcomes in India which underscores critical
competency, skill or infrastructural gaps at various stages of schooling.
Nationwide over 21.15 lakh students and 2.70 lakh teachers and school
leaders from more than 74,000 schools in 781 districts participated in the
assessment. National, State and District level reports for PARAKH Rashtriya
Sarvekshan 2024 are available at https://dashboard.parakh.ncert.gov.in/en,
adedicated dashboard designed to disseminate the findings of the assessment.
The findings of PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan 2024 highlight a
significant improvement when compared to National Achievement Survey
(NAS) 2021 scores in foundational literacy and numeracy skills, thereby,
reflecting the positive impact of the NIPUN Bharat Mission launched under
NEP 2020. Further, Central Government schools demonstrate the strongest
performance in all subjects at the preparatory and middle stage, suggesting
returns from improved infrastructure and increased per child spending in such
schools.

20.07.2026 848
following measures have been taken/proposed:
• Banks have been advised to give priority to eligible SC beneficiaries under
all bankable Government-sponsored schemes and ensure timely sanction and
disbursement of loans.
• Regular review meetings are being conducted under the State Level Bankers'
Committee (SLBC), District Consultative Committees (DCCs), and District
Level Review Committees (DLRCs) to monitor the progress of SC beneficiary
coverage and resolve implementation issues.
• Awareness programmes are being organized to improve financial inclusion
and increase institutional credit access for Scheduled Caste beneficiaries.
• Banks have been advised to simplify documentation, expedite appraisal, and
minimize delays in loan processing and disbursement.
• Pending loan applications are being reviewed periodically in DCC meetings,
and banks are advised to dispose of eligible applications within the prescribed
timelines.
• The progress of SC beneficiary coverage under various schemes is
monitored regularly by SLBC Andhra Pradesh, and corrective measures are
taken wherever gaps are identified.
• Capacity-building and financial literacy initiatives are being undertaken to
create awareness among SC beneficiaries regarding available credit-linked
schemes and banking services.

(a): National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) was launched in August
2016. The scheme was extended to continue as NAPS-2 from FY 2022-23.
Under, NAPS 2.0, the stipend support by Government of India (GoI) is paid
through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the bank account of apprentices. The
number of apprentices engaged in the State of Andhra Pradesh from FY 2022-23
till FY 2026-27 (upto 30.06.2026) is 93,094. The details of district-wise and year-
wise apprentices engaged in the State of Andhra Pradesh are given in the
enclosed Statement-I.

conducted within an establishment/industry. The number of establishment/
industries in Andhra Pradesh which have engaged apprentices under NAPS 2.0
(FY 2022-23 till FY 2026-27 (upto 30.06.2026)) are 1,135 unique establishments.
The district-wise, year-wise and sector-wise details of establishment/ industries
which have engaged apprentices in the State of Andhra Pradesh are given in the
enclosed Statement-II and III.

Andhra Pradesh are given in the enclosed Statement-I and IV.

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):
(a): Scheme of Samagra Shiksha supports State/UTs for various infrastructure
interventions like opening /strengthening of Schools, upgradation of schools,
additional classrooms, toilets, drinking water, electrification, different labs, various
residential facilities including KGBVs, NSCBAVs, PM JANMAN and DAJGUA etc.
To promote Digital Education, ICT/Smart classes, internet connectivity, digital
library are also supported. Under Skill/Vocational Education intervention, financial
assistance is provided to States/UTs for giving exposure to Skill Education to
students of Grades 6 to 8 and introduction of Skill courses from Grades 9 to 12,
which are aligned with the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF).

To cater to needs of educationally unserved/ underserved areas, the
Ministry of Education has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar
Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA) scheme, which envisages improvement in
access, equity and excellence in State Higher Education system through
support under various components viz., Multi- Disciplinary Education and
Research Universities (MERU), Grants to Strengthen Universities (Accredited
& Unaccredited Universities), Grants to Strengthen Colleges (Accredited &
Unaccredited Colleges), New Model Degree Colleges and Gender Inclusion
and Equity Initiatives. The government has launched the third phase of
Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) in June 2023 in the form of
Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA) with an outlay of Rs.
12926.10 crore, including the committed liabilities of the earlier phase of
RUSA, for the period 2023-24 to 2025-26, to cater to the needs of
educationally unserved/ underserved areas. Under the scheme, 613 units have
been approved with a total amount of Rs.8,168.51 crore.

notified the National Higher Education Qualifications Framework (NHEQF),

facilitates credit accumulation and transfer across academic, vocational and
skill education, while the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) supports seamless
academic mobility. UGC has also issued Guidelines for
Internship/Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programmes (IEDP), enabling
undergraduate students to acquire industry-relevant skills through structured
internships and apprenticeships integrated with their degree programmes.

technical education. It partners with industries and institutions to offer online
skill courses aligned with the regular curriculum, along with skill-focused
programmes, compulsory internships, and vocational degrees such as
Bachelor of Vocation (B.Voc). These initiatives are designed to build students’
practical abilities and improve employability. Additionally, AICTE has signed
MoUs with leading industries and organisations to support internships, skill-
building, and faculty upskilling, including hands-on exposure to Industry 4.0
technologies.
Employability Skill module has been included as a part of Job
Roles/SWAYAM courses in the curriculum which includes Communication
Skills, Self-Management Skills, Information and Communication Technology
Skills, Entrepreneurship Skills, and Green Skills.

The National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) bridges the gap
between academic learning and industry requirements by providing structured
on-the-job training to graduates and diploma holders. The Scheme promotes
industry-integrated education through Apprenticeship Embedded Degree
Programmes (AEDP), supports apprenticeships in emerging areas such as
Artificial Intelligence (AI), and facilitates academic credit integration through the
NATS Assessment and Creditisation Framework. During the last five financial
years, over 12.94 lakh apprentices have been engaged under the Scheme.
The NATS 2.0 Portal, launched on 30.07.2024, has further strengthened the
apprenticeship ecosystem by enabling participation of over 11,355 Higher
Education Institutions and more than 15,840 establishments.

TIGER AND ELEPHANT POPULATION
156. SHRIMATI JUNE MALIAH:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleas
ed to state:
(a) the latest population of tigers and elephants in the country;
(b) whether there has been any increase or decline in their population during the
last three years;
(c) the number of deaths of tigers and elephants due to poaching, train accidents
and electrocution during the said period; and
(d) the measures taken by the Government to prevent such death?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST
AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):
(a) and (b): The tiger population has increased as per the All India Tiger
Estimation done in 2022, with an estimated number of 3682 (range 3167-3925) as
compared to the 2018 estimation of 2967 (range 2603-3346) and the details are
given in the enclosed Statement-I.
The State-wise details of wild elephants in the country, as per the latest
“Status of Elephants in India: DNA-Based Synchronous All India Population
Estimation (SAIEE) 2022-25” are given in the enclosed Statement-II. This
nationwide estimate uses DNA-based mark–recapture for the first time in India.

interaction meetings etc. to encourage greater participation of industries and

(a) whether the Government has adopted any policy or criteria for equitable
establishment of Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) across the States
and Union Territories, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether Telangana, despite being in existence for over a decade, remains
one of the major States without an IIM and if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the Government has received any proposal from the Government of
Telangana for establishment of an IIM in the State, including an offer of about
200 acres of land free of cost and if so, the present status thereof;
(d) whether the Government proposes to establish an IIM in Telangana to
ensure balanced regional access to premier management education; and
(e) if so, the time-frame envisaged for its establishment and if not, the reasons
therefor?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION; AND
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH
EASTERN REGION (DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR):
(a) and (b): The Government of India periodically establishes new institutions of
national importance, including Indian Institutes of Management (IIM), across
India, after taking into account regional balance and resource availability.
Presently, there are 22 IIMs functioning in 21 States. The states of Telangana,
Goa, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim do not have an
IIM.

measures for air quality improvement, including sector-wise interventions for
control of vehicular emissions, construction and demolition (C&D) waste, road
dust, biomass burning, and industrial emissions. State action plan of Chhattisgarh
includes the interventions related to ‘emission due to burning of agro residues’
which are implemented and monitored at the State level.

Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandna Yojana (PMMVY), etc.
Apart from the above, eShram has linkages with National Career Service
(NCS) for Job Opportunities, Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) for Skill Development,
Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) for Pension and convergence
portal of MoHUA.
The Government is utilizing the eShram database as a national repository
of unorganised workers to facilitate their identification and integration with various
social security and welfare schemes such as Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri
Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-
SYM), National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), etc. The eShram
database enables targeted identification and inclusion of eligible beneficiaries,
promotes portability of benefits for migrant workers and supports evidence-based
policy formulation, thereby expanding social security coverage and improving
access to benefits for unorganised workers across the country.

(a) to (d): The official data on Employment and Unemployment is collected
through Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), which is conducted by Ministry of
Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) since 2017-18.
The latest PLFS report is the first in the series of Annual report conducted
during the calendar year (January 2025-December 2025). As per the report, the
estimated Unemployment Rate (UR) on usual status for youth of age 15-29 years
has decreased from 10.3% in 2024 to 9.9% in 2025 in the country. State/UT-wise
and year-wise information is available in the PLFS reports which may be seen at
the website of MoSPI at https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports.
The KLEMS database published by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) provides
employment estimates, including manufacturing sector, at all India level. As per
the latest data of the database, employment in the country increased to 64.33
crore in 2023-24 as compared to 47.5 crore in 2017-18. Total increase in
employment during 2017-18 to 2023-24 is about 16.83 crore (provisional) which
translate into 2.8 crore employment per year.

Act, CSR is a Board driven process and the Board of the company is empowered
to plan, decide, execute and monitor CSR activities of the company based on the
recommendation of its CSR Committee. This Committee formulates and
recommends the CSR policy, which outlines the activities to be undertaken by the
company in alignment with the areas or subjects specified in Schedule VII of the
Act. The first proviso to Section 135 (5) of the Act provides that the company shall
give preference to the local area and areas around it where it operates. However,
the emphasis on local area is only directory and not mandatory in nature and
companies need to balance local area preference with national priorities. The
Government does not issue any specific direction to the companies to spend in
any particular geographical area or for any particular activity.
All data related to CSR filed by companies in MCA21 registry including
State-wise, District-wise, year-wise, Development Sector-wise, project-wise and
company–wise, are available in public domain and can be accessed at
www.csr.gov.in. On the basis of annual filings made by companies in the MCA 21
registry, the Sector-wise details of CSR expenditure in Nashik for the last five
Financial Years (FY) i.e. FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25 is given in the enclosed
Statement.

(a) to (d): Education is in the concurrent list and both the Central Government and
State Governments work together for its improvement. The Government of India
has launched the PM-Vidyalaxmi, a new central sector scheme in November
2024. Any student, who gets merit-based admission in top Quality Higher

All the top 100 ranked HEIs in the overall/ category-specific and/or domain
specific rankings in the list of National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) list;
plus all the top 200 ranked HEIs under the governance of State/UT governments
in the list of NIRF; plus all remaining HEIs under the governance of Government
of India are included in the list of QHEIs. A total of 1051 QHEIs, including 138
QHEIs from the state of Tamil Nadu have been included under the PM Vidyalaxmi
Scheme.
Further, for students with annual family income up to ₹8 lakh, the scheme
provides 3% interest subvention on loans up to ₹10 lakh. Each year up to one
lakh fresh students not getting any other scholarship or interest subvention on
education loan will get this interest subvention benefit. An outlay of ₹ 3,600 crore
has been made from 2024-25 to 2030-31, for providing 3% interest subvention
benefit for up to 7 lakh fresh students during this period.
The State-wise and year-wise number of PM-Vidyalaxmi education loans
and amount sanctioned along with Institute-wise number of students from the
state of Tamil Nadu who have benefitted under the scheme since its launch is
given in the enclosed Statement.

and the reasons therefor?

2.0 (SD2.0), Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD), and Special
Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI).
Sanctioned projects for the state of Sikkim under the SASCI scheme in
the financial year 2024-25 include the Skywalk, Bhaleydhunga, Yangang in
Namchi and Border Experience in Nathula. These projects are expected to be
developed in a period of 2 years. Further, under the CBDD sub-scheme,
projects for "Kabi Chronicles: A journey through Unity and Heritage" and
"Echoes of Valor: The Gnathang Valley Experience” were also sanctioned in
the financial year 2024-25.

comprehensive action to address emission from burning of waste, burning of

areas.

coastal communities only through non-mechanized manual methods under
both the CRZ Notification, 2019 and the Island Coastal Regulation Zone
(ICRZ) Notification, 2019. The State Governments and Union territory
Administration may permit such removal of sand in the specified time period in

TOURISM DEVELOPMENT IN BIHAR
205. SHRI RAJA RAM SINGH:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has undertaken an assessment of tourism
infrastructure gaps across major heritage and religious destinations in
Bihar, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the details of the funds released and utilised under Central tourism
schemes in Bihar during the last five years; and
(c) whether the Government is considering any major programme to develop
tourism in Rohtas district of Bihar and if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI
GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT):
(a): Development of tourism infrastructure, amenities and experiences at
tourist destinations is primarily undertaken by the concerned State
Government and Union Territory Administration. However, the Ministry of
Tourism, under its various schemes such as Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and
Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD), Swadesh Darshan (SD),
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0), Challenge Based Destination Development
(CBDD) provides financial assistance for the development of tourism
infrastructure across the country including Bihar.
(b): The details of the funds released and utilized for the projects under the
said schemes in Bihar are given in the enclosed Statement.

(d): Under Samagra Shiksha, there is a dedicated Inclusive Education
component for various interventions such as Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya
(KGBVs) residential schools from class VI to XII, for girls belonging to
disadvantaged groups such as SC, ST, OBC, Minority and Below Poverty Line
(BPL), Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Avasiya Vidyalayas which provide
residential facilities for both girls and boys belonging to Socio Economically
Disadvantaged Groups (SEDGs). Further, the educational needs of children
from the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) are addressed through
the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) and
Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) Schemes, provision of
transport allowance and undertaking enrolment & retention drives.
Special training for age-appropriate admission of out of school children
and residential as well as non-residential training for older children, seasonal
hostels / residential camps, special training centres at worksites, transport/
escort facility etc. are also supported to bring out of school children to the
formal schooling system.

Act, 2009, provision for free textbooks and uniforms are provided to children
from SEDGs. Further, Section 12 of RTE Act, 2009 provides for 25% seats to
be provided to EWS category of students in private-unaided schools. Further,

(a) to (e): The Navodaya Vidyalaya Scheme envisages for opening of one
Navodaya Vidyalaya (NV) in each district of the country. Opening of new NVs
is a continuous process which depends on the willingness of the concerned
State Government/UT administration to make available requisite suitable land,
free of cost, for construction of the permanent building and making available
required temporary building, free of rent, to run the Vidyalaya till the permanent
building is constructed. Sanction and opening of new NVs depends on
approval by the competent authority as per extant procedures. As on date, a
total of 694 NVs have been sanctioned across the country, including 28
additional NVs.
At present, 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh have been covered under
Navodaya Vidyalaya Scheme. Further, two additional NVs, which were
sanctioned in Prakasam (now Markapuram) and East Godavari (now
Polavaram) on basis of SC/ST concentrated areas, are also functional. Thus,
total 15 NVs are functional in the State. List of NVs in the State of Andhra
Pradesh is given in the enclosed Statement.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, vide its judgment dated
01.09.2025, inter alia, held that the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) is one of the
minimum qualifications prescribed under Section 23 of the Right of Children to
Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, and is mandatory for
appointment as a teacher in schools covered under the Act. The order of the
Hon'ble Supreme Court may be accessed at the following link:
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/36466/36466_2018_9_1501_63
764_Judgement_01- Sep-2025 pdf.
Subsequently, while disposing of the review petitions in the matter, vide
judgment dated 29.05.2026 the Hon'ble Supreme Court extended the timeline
for acquisition of TET qualification from 31.08.2027 to 31.08.2028. The
judgment dated 29.05.2026 of the Hon'ble Supreme Court may be accessed at
the following link:
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/53434/53434_2025_7_1501_71637_J
udgement_29-May-2026.pdf
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the judgment dated 29.05.2026, has
further observed that the respective appropriate Governments/authorities
should endeavour to conduct the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) periodically,
preferably twice every year, with an interval of approximately six months
between successive examinations, so as to afford eligible teachers a
reasonable opportunity to comply with the prescribed minimum qualification.

(TET), is maintained by the respective State Governments and Union Territory

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, vide its judgment dated
01.09.2025, inter alia, held that the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) is one of the
minimum qualifications prescribed under Section 23 of the Right of Children to
Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, and is mandatory for
appointment as a teacher in schools covered under the Act. The order of the
Hon'ble Supreme Court may be accessed at the following link:
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/36466/36466_2018_9_1501_63
764_Judgement_01- Sep-2025 pdf.
Subsequently, while disposing of the review petitions in the matter, vide
judgment dated 29.05.2026 the Hon'ble Supreme Court extended the timeline
for acquisition of TET qualification from 31.08.2027 to 31.08.2028. The
judgment dated 29.05.2026 of the Hon'ble Supreme Court may be accessed at
the following link:
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/53434/53434_2025_7_1501_71637_J
udgement_29-May-2026.pdf
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the judgment dated 29.05.2026, has
further observed that the respective appropriate Governments/authorities
should endeavour to conduct the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) periodically,
preferably twice every year, with an interval of approximately six months
between successive examinations, so as to afford eligible teachers a
reasonable opportunity to comply with the prescribed minimum qualification.

UNIFIED PENSION SCHEME
218. SHRI HASMUKHBHAI SOMABHAI PATEL:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of retired Central Government subscribers eligible to
claim additional benefits under the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS);
(b) the number of claims received and processed so far under the UPS since
its introduction;
(c) whether the Government has plans to extend similar benefits to other
pension schemes or sectors in the near future; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PANKAJ
CHOUDHARY):
(a): There are 25,756 retired Central Government subscribers eligible to
receive additional benefits under Unified Pension Scheme (UPS).
(b): As on 9th July, 2026, 12,258 claims have been received and out of which
9,823 claims have been processed for payment of benefits under UPS.
(c) and (d): UPS has been introduced as an option under National Pension
System (NPS) for the employees of Central Government who are covered
under the NPS. There is no proposal under consideration to extend such
benefits to other pension schemes or sectors.

sector have been examined by the Commission under the enforcement and
combination provisions of the Competition Act, 2002 (“Act”).
In assessing combinations involving the telecom and cement sectors,
the Commission considers the factors specified under Section 20(4) of the
Act. These include, inter alia, the parties’ market shares and the degree of
concentration in the relevant market. The Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (“HHI”)
is also used, wherever appropriate, as one of the analytical tools for
assessing market concentration. Such indicators are considered alongside the
specific facts and market conditions of each case.
(c): The Market Study on the Telecom Sector in India highlights competition
concerns relating to barriers to entry arising from high spectrum costs and
data-driven network effects, and observes that competition issues arising from
digital markets, data leverage, privacy, and vertical integration require case-
by-case assessment under the Competition Act, 2002. The study does not
record any specific finding of collusive conduct and notes that existing vertical
integration was generally viewed by stakeholders as pro-competitive and not
posing any imminent competition concern.

decided 29 combination cases in the telecom sector and 15 combination cases
in the cement sector. During the same period, the CCI directed investigations
in 3 cases relating to the telecom sector and 4 cases relating to the cement
sector. CCI has also passed final orders in 6 cases each relating to the
telecom and cement sectors during this period.

mosaic of diverse ecosystems, including forests, wetlands, grasslands,
scrublands, rivers, and other natural habitats. These interconnected
ecosystems collectively support rich biodiversity, sustain ecological processes,
regulate hydrological and climatic functions, and provide a wide range of
ecosystem services. Accordingly, conservation and management of forest
areas are undertaken through an integrated landscape approach that
recognizes the ecological interdependence of these various ecosystems.

undertaken with scientific and technical approach ensuring heterogeneous mix
of native plant species. Apart from plantations the same principle is followed in
seed sowing of grasses, sedges and seed sowing along soil moisture
conservation structures. This is done to ensure a stratified, multi species floral
composition in the forest which in turn supports faunal biodiversity. Such
afforestation, forest restoration and biodiversity conservation programmes, with
due emphasis on conservation of natural forests, restoration of degraded forest
landscapes with use of locally suitable indigenous species, and enhancement
of ecosystem functions lead to rich biodiverse forests.
