the cultural and creative economy. The proposed strategy envisages
interventions for capacity building, market access, innovation, digital enablement
and institutional strengthening with a view to promoting sustainable growth of
the creative economy, including support for emerging artists and creative
practitioners.
(b): The proposed intervention broadly covers sectors such as visual arts,
performing arts, museums, cultural heritage, architecture, digital creative
industries and other creative services.
(c): The Ministry regularly engages with stakeholders, experts, cultural
institutions and other Ministries/Departments, as and when required, for policy
formulation and implementation of its programmes.

of cultural heritage, support to artists and cultural institutions, organization of
cultural events, and international cultural exchanges, which contribute to
employment and livelihood opportunities in the cultural sector.

heritage, tourism, cultural exchanges and livelihood opportunities across the
country, including the State of Maharashtra. No State-specific assessment of the
contribution of the cultural and creative sector to economic growth or cultural
diplomacy is maintained by the Ministry.

Centres (MCCs) in collaboration with States/Institutions to deliver career related

Funds under PMKVY are released to implementing agencies for meeting
the training cost as per prescribed norms. Under JSS scheme, funds are
released to Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) directly. Under NAPS,
stipend support up to Rs 1500/- per month is released to apprentices through
DBT and not to establishments covered. Day to day administration as well as
financial control in respect of ITIs, lies with the respective State Government/

An independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 was
conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management
(AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of
India. As per the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift
in employment outcomes for short term training (STT) candidates. The
combined share of employed and self-employed STT respondents increased
from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8
percentage point increase. Income- related outcomes also show positive
movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of Recognition of Prior
Learning (RPL) candidates reporting an increase in income following training
and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded access to
formal skill training and certification and has generated measurable
improvements in skill confidence, employment participation, and income
outcomes for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries.

the PMKK guidelines, PMKKs were supported through target allocations under
the PMKVY scheme for a period of three years, after which they were
expected to become self-sustainable. During this period, PMKKs were also
permitted to implement Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)-funded training

The following steps have been taken by the Government to enhance
industry participation, apprenticeship opportunities, improve placement and
employment outcomes under the Skill India Mission:
i. National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has
approved 10209 qualifications as per the industry requirements, including
2975 valid and active qualifications.
ii. 36 Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry leaders in the respective
sectors, have been set up which are mandated to identify the skill
development needs of respective sectors as well as to determine skill
competency standards. NSDC, under the market-led program, provides
support to training providers that collaborate and align skill courses with
industry demand.
iii. Under PMKVY, the new age/future skills job-roles have been specially
aligned with Industry 4.0 requirements in areas like AI/ML, Robotics,
Mechatronics, Drone Technology, etc. for upcoming market demand and
industry requirements.

under Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives. These
partnerships facilitate the provision of technical and professional skills
training in modern technologies.

up to Rs 1500/- per month is released to beneficiaries through Direct
Benefit Transfer (DBT).
v. DGT is implementing the Flexi MoU Scheme and Dual System of Training
(DST), which are meant to provide training to ITI students in an industrial
environment as per their requirements.
vi. Government of India has signed Memorandum of Understanding
(MoU)/Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) in the field of skill development
and vocational education and training with fourteen countries to align the
skilling efforts as per the global requirements.
vii. General of Training (DGT) under the aegis of MSDE has introduced 32
new age /future skills courses in Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and
National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) under CTS to provide training in
emerging areas such as 5G Network Technician, Artificial Intelligence
Programming assistant, Cyber Security Assistant, Drone Technician etc.
viii. DGT has signed MoU with IT Tech companies like IBM, CISCO, Future
Skill Rights Network, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft to
ensure industry linkages for the institutes at the state and regional levels
under Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives. These
partnerships facilitate the provision of technical and professional skills
training in modern technologies.

payment to farmers in Kerala
SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURESH (MAVELIKKARA): I wish to draw the attention
of the Government to the difficulties faced by paddy farmers in Kerala,
particularly in Kuttanad, one of the country's most important rice-producing
regions, under the existing Paddy Receipt Sheet (PRS)-based payment
mechanism. Under the Decentralised Procurement (DCP) Scheme, farmers
receive payment through bank loans against PRS instead of direct payment for
the paddy procured. Although the State Government guarantees repayment,
farmers are treated as borrowers, adversely affecting their CIBIL scores and
limiting their access to institutional credit. I urge the Government to consider
enabling the Food Corporation of India (FCI) to procure paddy directly from
farmers in Kerala, especially in Kuttanad, and ensure direct payment within 3–
7 days. Alternatively, the PRS mechanism should be delinked from the
individual farmer's CIBIL records so that farmers are not shown as bank
borrowers for Government-guaranteed procurement payments. Such

(xxii) Regarding likely adverse impact on Tamil Nadu due to proposed
construction of Mekedatu Balancing Reservoir on River Cauvery
by Karnataka
DR. KALANIDHI VEERASWAMY (CHENNAI NORTH): I would like to draw
the attention of the Government towards a matter of urgent public importance
regarding the proposed construction of the Mekedatu Balancing Reservoir
Project by the Government of Karnataka across the River Cauvery. The
proposed project has caused widespread concern in Tamil Nadu, as it has the
potential to adversely affect the assured flow of Cauvery waters to the lower
riparian state. Tamil Nadu's farmers, particularly those in the Cauvery Delta
region, are critically dependent on the timely release of Cauvery waters for
irrigation, drinking water needs, and sustaining agricultural livelihoods. The
Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal, in its final award, and the judgment of the
Hon'ble Supreme Court have determined the allocation of Cauvery waters
among the basin States. The Cauvery basin has been recognized as a water-
deficit basin, and any new storage project undertaken without the concurrence
of the co-basin states and without the approval of the competent statutory
authorities would raise serious concerns regarding the implementation of the
existing legal framework governing inter-state river water sharing. The
Government of Tamil Nadu and the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly have
consistently opposed the Mekedatu project, maintaining that it could prejudice
the legitimate and legally protected water rights of the lower riparian state and
adversely impact millions of farmers and citizens dependent on the Cauvery

(xxiii) Need to address the problems being faced by employees of BSNL
in the country
SHRI BASTIPATI NAGARAJU (KURNOOL): I would like to highlight the
urgent crisis facing the employees of BSNL. This public sector organisation is
the backbone of India’s telecom network, connecting our most remote and
rural areas. During national emergencies, natural disasters, and the COVID-19
pandemic, BSNL workers served with absolute dedication. Tragically, over 380
of these workers lost their lives while keeping our nation connected. Yet, their
immense sacrifices remain completely unrewarded. Today, these employees'
rightful salary hike under the 3rd Pay Revision Commission has been delayed
for years. Retirees are waiting indefinitely for their pensions to be updated. Pay
and promotions between different categories of staff and their medical benefits
have been deeply cut. Therefore, I request the hon’ble Government to grant
an immediate waiver of the affordability clause for the implementation of 3rd
PRC and finalise wage negotiation for non-executives; delink pension revision
from profitability and ensure parity with Central Government pensioners; and
ensure one-time pension option under CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972 for those
recruited by DoT before BSNL’s formation. Justice for BSNL employees is not
only a matter of policy, it is a matter of honouring national service.

STATEMENT
(a) and (b) : Market Development Assistance (MDA) is implemented on pan India
basis.
Under this Scheme, the Government has approved assistance @ ₹1500/MT
to promote organic carbon enhancers i.e., Fermented Organic Fertilizers (FOM)
and Liquid FOM; and organic fertilizer i.e., Phosphate Rich Organic Manure
(PROM), produced at plants under the Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro
Resources Dhan (GOBARdhan) initiative, covering different biogas/CBG plants.
Under the scheme, 133 Compressed Bio Gas(CBG)/Bio Gas (BG) plants have
been registered on the Integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS) portal as
on 23.03.2026 for sale of FOM/LFOM/PROM. CBG/BG plants can claim MDA on
FOM/LFOM/PROM sold through PoS (Point of Sale) to Farmers/Farmers
Cooperatives/Farmers Producers Organisations (FPOs)/Panchayats/District
Development Authorities (DDAs)/Central Public Work Department (CPWD)/Govt.

Financial & Physical Status:
The State Implementing Agency, Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation,
as on 28.02.2026, has utilised ₹341.44 crore out of the two instalments of ₹300

The present status of progress of the CIF under Gujarat bulk drug park is as
under:
 The environmental clearance was granted to the Gujarat Bulk Drug Park in
February 2024. All the common infrastructure facilities related civil tenders,
such as road, drainage, water infrastructure, effluent collection and rack
system are awarded and approximately most of the work has been
completed on site.
 CIF Utility tenders like Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP), Solvent
Recovery, Treatment Storage & Disposal Facilities, have also been
awarded and a small portion of the work has been completed on site.
Tender of parking has been awarded in November, 2025.
 Tender of Steam Generation is released and which is under evaluation.

(Source: UAS, GKVK, Bengaluru)
Practical Significance:
 Applying the optimal dose of fertilizers integrated with organic sources
such as FYM is essential for sustaining crop productivity and improving
long-term soil health.
 Indiscriminate or imbalanced use of nitrogenous fertilizers drastically
reduces yield and leads to significant deterioration of soil health.
 Farmers should be discouraged from applying only nitrogen and
phosphorus fertilizers (such as DAP and urea) for finger millet. The
inclusion of potassium, along with recommended doses of nitrogen and
phosphorus, is crucial for achieving sustained higher yields.
 The commonly used high-analysis fertilizer DAP should be
supplemented with secondary nutrients, as continuous reliance on DAP
alone has contributed to widespread secondary nutrient deficiencies.
 Continuous application of the recommended dose of phosphorus has
been observed to cause soil phosphorus buildup. In such situations,
applying half the recommended phosphorus dose is sufficient to meet
the crop's needs without compromising yield.

authorities in Saudi Arabia.

ASEAN INDIA RELATIONS
5528. SHRI RAO RAJENDRA SINGH:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the details of progress made in the culmination of ASEAN-India Trade in
Goods Agreement (AITIGA);
(b) whether, in light of recent geopolitical turbulence, both stakeholders are
working towards enhanced trade and maritime cooperation; and
(c) if so, the details of such a future roadmap for the same?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST
AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):
(a) to (c) : The ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) was signed
on 13th August 2009 and came into force on 1st January 2010 in respect of
India, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand. By 1st August 2011, all ASEAN
members became signatory to the FTA. India and ASEAN are constructively
engaged in the review of ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA).
India and ASEAN are maritime neighbours. To strengthen maritime
cooperation, ASEAN-INDIA JOINT STATEMENT ON MARITIME

(a) and (b) : As per the data obtained from the National Registry for Rare and
Other Inherited Disorders (NRROID) maintained by the Indian Council of Medical
Research (ICMR), since 2019, around 4749 Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy

184 DMD patients are reported as deceased in the Registry. State/UT-wise
distribution of this data is given in the enclosed Statement.
(c) : DMD is categorized as a rare disease under the National Policy for Rare
Diseases (NPRD), 2021 framed by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Health being a State subject, the primary responsibility of providing healthcare
services is that of the State Governments. However, to mitigate the challenges
posed by rare diseases in India, the policy provides financial and medical
assistance for treatment of patients suffering from identified rare diseases in the
designated Centers of Excellence (CoEs). Following measures have already been
taken to address the DMD issue:
 The limit of financial assistance provided by NPRD for treatment of rare
disease has increased from ₹20 lakhs to ₹50 lakhs per patient. Rare
Disease Committee of the CoEs decides treatment and fund allocation after
clinical examination on case-to-case basis.
 Since the inception of the NPRD, the number of CoEs has increased from 8
to 15 and the number of rare diseases covered under the policy has
increased from 51 to 63.

The details of the initiatives taken to improve nutritional status of children,
adolescent girls and mothers under Mission Poshan 2.0 in the country including
the State of Tamil Nadu are as below:
Under Mission Poshan 2.0, a new strategy has been made for

reduction in malnutrition and for improved health, wellness and
immunity through activities like community engagement, outreach,
behavioural change and advocacy. It focuses on Maternal Nutrition,
Infant and Young Child Feeding Norms, treatment of Severe Acute
Malnutrition (SAM)/ Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) and wellness
through AYUSH practices to reduce prevalence of wasting, stunting,
anaemia and being underweight.
Supplementary Nutrition is provided to Children (6 months to 6 years),

Pregnant Women, Lactating Mothers and Adolescent Girls (age 14-18
years) in accordance with the nutrition norms contained in Schedule-II
of the National Food Security Act, 2013. Greater emphasis is being
laid on the use of millets at least once a week for preparation of Hot
Cooked Meal and Take-Home ration at Anganwadi Centers.
Further, Ministries of Women & Child Development and Health &

Family Welfare have jointly released the ‘Protocol for Management of
Malnutrition in Children’ to prevent and treat severely acute
malnutrition in children.

Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region
(MOVCDNER) for the North Eastern States since 2015-16. Both schemes stress
on end-to-end support to farmers engaged in organic farming i.e. from production
to processing, certification and marketing. Primary focus of the schemes is to form
organic clusters, with preference to small and marginal farmers, to create a supply
chain. Both the schemes are implemented through States /UT Governments.
Under PKVY, assistance of Rs. 31,500 per ha is provided over 3 years for
promotion of organic farming. Out of this, assistance of Rs. 15,000 per ha is
provided to farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer for on- farm /off –farm organic
inputs including organic compost. Financial assistance of Rs. 4,500/ha is
provided over 3 years for marketing, packaging, branding, value addition etc. Rs.
3,000/ha for 3 years is provided for certification. Assistance is also provided @Rs.
9,000/ha in 3 years for training, awareness & capacity building.
Achievements of PKVY Scheme since its inception (as on 31.12.2025):
18.84 lakh hectares area has been covered.

33.94 lakh farmers benefited from the scheme.

Since 2015-16, a total of ₹2548.99 crore (central share) has been released

under PKVY Scheme (as of 31.12.2025).
Achievement of PKVY in Andhra Pradesh (as on 31.12.2025):

524769 hectares of land have been converted to organic farming.

1129931 farmers have benefitted under the scheme.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS (SHRIMATI ANUPRIYA PATEL):
(a) to (e) : National Medical Commission Act, 2019 empowers State Medical
Council (SMC)/Ethics and Medical Registration Board (EMRB) to take
disciplinary action in respect of any professional or ethical misconduct by a
registered medical practitioner in accordance with the regulations/guidelines
framed under the Act. Accordingly, the NMC forwards the complaint to
concerned State Health Departments and SMCs for appropriate action.
The Act provides for an opportunity of hearing to the RMP before taking any
action against him. Provision for an appeal against the decision of SMC/EMRB
has also been made.
Further, the rules framed under clause (d)(i) of sub-section (2) of Section
33 of the Bengal Medical Act, 1914, deal with the conduct of enquiries in
complaint cases of the West Bengal Medical Council (WBMC). Additionally, the
WBMC has informed that from 2016 to date, a total of 849 complaints of
medical negligence have been received/reported.

MWCD in convergence with Ministry of Skill Development and
Entrepreneurship (MSDE) is implementing NAVYA (Nurturing Aspirations through
Vocational Training for Young Adolescent Girls), a special pilot project for skilling of
Adolescent Girls (AGs) in the age group of 16-18 years and passed secondary
level of school education pursuant to the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)
signed between MWCD with MSDE on 11th October, 2022 for bringing greater
convergence in Skill Development Initiatives targeted at Young Girls especially in
non-traditional skills.
Under NAVYA, 27 districts across 19 States and UT including Fatehpur and
Sonbhadra districts of State of Uttar Pradesh have been selected for Skilling of
Adolescent Girls (AGs). As on 20th March, 2026, a total of 813 AGs have
completed their training in various selected districts across the country. Regular
monitoring of NAVYA project is undertaken through VCs and sustained
engagements with States and UT concerned.

FSSAI has established a network of food testing laboratories across India for
the analysis of food to ensure the compliance with the quality and safety standards.
As on date, there are 252 National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration
Laboratories (NABL) notified for analysis of food samples and 24 Referral Food
Laboratories for the analysis of appellate samples. In the State of Karnataka,
FSSAI has notified 20 primary laboratories including 3 State Food Testing
Laboratories (SFTLs) at Belagavi, Mysuru and Bangalore and 2 referral food
testing laboratories (Details are given in the enclosed Statement).
FSSAI has also provided funds for Mobile Food Testing Laboratory (MFTL)
referred to as “Food Safety on Wheels” (FSW) to States/UTs. It is an important
means to combat adulteration as FSWs are equipped with basic infrastructure for
on the spot testing of adulteration in various food commodities. Currently, 1 MFTL
is deployed in State of Karnataka for on the spot testing of common adulterants.
FSSAI extends financial and technical assistance to States/UTs for
strengthening of food safety infrastructure in the country. The support includes
the following:
 Strengthening Enforcement and Compliance such as Licensing and
Registration
 Inspections and Audits, Sampling and Testing of Enforcement and
Surveillance Samples
 Consumer Grievance Redressal

areas and for their residential quarters so that they find it attractive to serve
in public health facilities in such areas.

Pediatricians & Anesthetist/ Life Saving Anaesthesia Skills (LSAS) trained
doctors is also provided to increase availability of specialists for conducting
Cesarean Sections in rural & remote area.

courses for staff serving in difficult areas and improving accommodation
arrangement in rural areas have also been introduced under NHM.

to deliver universal, free comprehensive primary healthcare services,
with a focus on wellness and the delivery of an expanded range of

for outpatient care, dispensing medicines, diagnostic services,
adequate spaces to display communication material of health messages,
including audio-visual aids and appropriate community spaces for
wellness activities, including the practice of Yoga and physical
exercises.

12. XV-Finance Commission Health Grants channelized through local
government - The XV Finance Commission recommended grants
through local governments, allocating ₹70,051 crores over five years
from FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26 to strengthen primary healthcare. This
funding supports various rural healthcare components, including the
development of building-less sub-centres, primary health centres
(PHCs), and community health centres (CHCs). It also facilitates the
conversion of rural PHCs and sub-health centres (SHCs) into Ayushman
Arogya Mandir, enhances diagnostic infrastructure in primary healthcare
facilities, and establishes Block-Level Public Health Units, with a special
focus on tribal areas and aspirational districts.
13. To enhance availability of specialists, NHM offers flexible provisions,
which include the following:
 The GoI support States in recruiting and retaining specialists in
public health facilities through the innovative “You Quote, We Pay”
scheme under NHM, which allows specialists to negotiate
lucrative and flexible salaries. There are also provisions for
engaging specialists on a per-case basis if required.
 To address shortages in difficult and underserved areas, provision
for differential salaries based on the place of posting are available
under NHM. Many States have categorized all their blocks and
facilities based on the difficulty level for providing services there.

requirements. Globally, this shift is already underway. Facing similar capacity
crunches, Japan and Argentina recently raised their pilot retirement ages to 68
years, and countries like Australia, New Zealand, and Canada have abolished
maximum age limits entirely for domestic operations. They prioritize rigorous
bi-annual medical, cognitive, and simulator assessments over an arbitrary
chronological number. While a First Officer can be trained relatively quickly,
developing a Captain requires thousands of flight hours. Raising the retirement
age keeps experienced pilots in command longer, giving younger pilots more
time to safely upgrade. Economically, this extension also drastically reduces
Indian airlines' reliance on expensive foreign expatriate pilots. Hence, I urge
the adoption of a similar health-based extension framework so that we can
meet growing passenger demand and maintain regional connectivity, while
ensuring absolute passenger safety and cost-effectiveness.

Crafts Mela in Haryana collapsed, killing a police inspector and injuring several
others. Similar risks exist in ziplines, bungee platforms, scuba boats and ATV
trails, where permissions are ad hoc and inspections are sporadic.

minimum standards, but they are not a statutory enforcement mechanism.

National Authority for Adventure Sports and Amusement Ride Safety to set
baseline standards, maintain a national operator registry, mandate third-party
safety audits and insurance, and run a compulsory incident-reporting database
with annual public reporting. This will hopefully ensure minimum safety
protection across States.

*SHRI BALWANT BASWANT WANKHEDE (AMRAVATI): Honorable
Chairperson Madam, my city of Amravati has fallen into the clutches of MD
drugs. Recently, the police administration conducted raids in which MD drugs
worth crores of rupees were seized. The police agency has carried out three or
four such raids; while the trail sometimes points to connections in Ahmedabad,
Gujarat, and at other times to Rajasthan, it is imperative to identify the
mastermind behind this operation. The young people of Amravati city have
become ensnared in the grip of drugs, and the government must take
appropriate measures to rescue them. The government has failed to provide a
satisfactory explanation regarding the exact source of these drugs. However,
the operations conducted in recent times suggest that Amravati may well be
the central hub for this illicit trade, from where these drugs could potentially be
distributed across the entire state of Maharashtra.
Honorable Chairperson Madam, therefore, I demand that both the
Central and State governments appoint a special task force to conduct a
thorough investigation into this matter, take decisive action, and eradicate this
drug menace from its very roots.

Chairperson Madam, my city of Amravati has fallen into the clutches of MD
drugs. Recently, the police administration conducted raids in which MD drugs
worth crores of rupees were seized. The police agency has carried out three or
four such raids; while the trail sometimes points to connections in Ahmedabad,
Gujarat, and at other times to Rajasthan, it is imperative to identify the
mastermind behind this operation. The young people of Amravati city have
become ensnared in the grip of drugs, and the government must take
appropriate measures to rescue them. The government has failed to provide a
satisfactory explanation regarding the exact source of these drugs. However,
the operations conducted in recent times suggest that Amravati may well be
the central hub for this illicit trade, from where these drugs could potentially be
distributed across the entire state of Maharashtra.
Honorable Chairperson Madam, therefore, I demand that both the
Central and State governments appoint a special task force to conduct a
thorough investigation into this matter, take decisive action, and eradicate this
drug menace from its very roots.

माननीय अ(cid:197)य (cid:177) : आइटम नंबर 20 A, िजितन (cid:255)साद जी।

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI JITIN
PRASADA): Hon. Speaker Sir, I move for leave to introduce a Bill to amend
certain enactments for decriminalising and rationalising offences to further
enhance trust-based governance for ease of living and doing business.
It seeks to enhance ease of doing business and ease of living by
decriminalising minor offences and implementing measures such as revising
fines and penalties proportionate to the offence, establishing adjudicating
officers and setting up appellate authorities. It proposes to amend 79 Central
Acts administered by 23 Ministries. A total of 784 provisions are being
proposed to be amended, out of which 717 provisions are being decriminalised
to foster ease of doing business, and 67 provisions are being proposed to
facilitate ease of living. This builds on the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of
Provisions) Act, 2023, which decriminalised 183 provisions under 42 Central
Acts, continuing efforts to streamline regulations and promote trust-based
governance.
 Published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part-II, Section 2, dated 27.03.2026.

I have been making efforts since 2007 to provide a permanent irrigation
solution to the people and farmers of drought affected districts of Karnataka
such as Chikkaballapur, Bangalore Rural and Kolar and other Bayaluseeme
(Plateau) districts of Karnnataka.
The previous BJP Government in Karnataka State had announced a
plan to ensure tertiary (third-stage) treated water to the people.
However, this initiative was cancelled by the present Government of
Karnataka as it is discontinued many other projects. Several scientific studies
have indicated that the adverse health among the people is caused by the
water, which is treated only two stages. Therefore, I would like to propose
three suggestions to consider in this regard.
A scientific guidelines issued by the Union government should be
implemented by the state government to ensure the water is treated at tertiary
level (third-stage) before it is released. And, the Yettinahole project works
should be expedited and completed at the earliest.
The allocation of 15 TMC of water share from the river Krishna should
be released to mitigate the water scarcity and save the precious lives of the
people of these districts.
Thanking you.

*ADV. GOWAAL KAGADA PADAVI (NANDURBAR): Honorable Chairperson
Madam, thank you. My parliamentary constituency of Nandurbar is recognized
as the number one district in the entire state of Maharashtra for papaya
production. However, despite such large-scale production, farmers still do not
receive fair prices for their produce. Through you, I would like to urge the
Central Government to establish an independent 'Papaya processing Park' in
my Nandurbar constituency. This park should be equipped with facilities for
papaya grading, washing, packaging, and storage. Furthermore, Nandurbar
should be included under the 'One Nation, One Product' scheme to garner
both national and international recognition. Financial assistance should be
extended to papaya-growing farmers through initiatives such as the PM Kisan
Sampada Scheme, the Mega Food Park Scheme, and APEDA. Additionally, a
skill development and training center should be established for tribal youth—
both young men and women—to generate local employment opportunities.
Cold storage facilities and logistics centers should also be set up within the
district. Hon. Madam, if this Papaya Park is established, it will benefit
thousands of farmers; their incomes will double, they will receive fair
remuneration for their produce, and their agricultural produce will no longer go
to waste. Moreover, market control will no longer remain solely in the hands of
traders, and the Papaya Park will accord Nandurbar recognition on a national
level. Therefore, I appeal to the Central Government to grant approval for this

Chairperson Madam. Today, I wish to express about an important matter
regarding my constituency. For the last 30 years, the survey work for our
Gopalpur – Rairakhol railway line has been conducted repeatedly, and even
now, ORIDL (Odisha Rail Infrastructure Development Ltd) has already
submitted its report to the Government.
However, it is a matter of great concern that this railway line, which
connects South Odisha with West Odisha via Kandhamal, remains an absolute
necessity but remained untouched till date. My parliamentary constituency is a
tribal-dominant area and an aspirational district; to this day, it remains the only
district in Odisha where the district headquarters has not been connected by a
railway line—that is Kandhamal district.

ensure that the Gopalpur – Rairakhol railway line is connected as soon as
possible.This project should be completed to ensure the economic progress
and livelihood of the countless tribal brothers, sisters, and people from
backward classes residing in this region. Thank you.

A simplified Registration Module for platform workers has been launched
on 12.03.2025 on the eShram portal to facilitate platform workers to register
themselves or update their occupation, if already registered on eShram portal.
To maximise registration of platform workers on eShram portal, three
nationwide special registration drives were held during the months of April,
May and August-September, 2025 in collaboration with States and Union
Territories. As on 14.07.2026, over 10.65 lakh platform workers are registered
on eShram portal.
The Ministry of Labour & Employment has conducted multiple rounds of
deliberations with Aggregators, Knowledge Partners, Platform Workers
Associations, State Government/Union Territories and other organisations for
social security framework of gig and platform workers to move forward for a
comprehensive welfare scheme for platform workers across the country, as
mandated under the Code.

Fund during FY 2020-21 till FY 2025-26;
(ii) Rs. 2,862.04 crore to the 82 non-attainment cities though Central Sector

State-wise details of funds provided under NCAP, are given in the enclosed

results with 108 cities showing reduction in PM10 concentration in 2025-26
with respect to 2017-18, 46 cities have shown reduction in PM10 levels by

achieved a reduction of more than 40%. A total of 14 Cities have met NAAQS
and have PM10 Concentrations less than 60 µg/m3. Details of air quality
improvement in 130 cities are given in the enclosed Statement-IV.

entrusted with the task of maintaining good industrial relations and protecting the
interest of workers including in matters relating to termination, retrenchment or
lay-off and its prevention.
The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 contains various provisions to
safeguard workers' rights and job security, including statutory safeguards in the
form of mandatory notice period, retrenchment compensation and provision for
retrenched workers to be given preference in re-employment are applicable for
all retrenched workers. The Code also introduces Workers Re-skilling fund for
training of retrenched workers for the first time with a view to providing financial
support to retrenched workers to utilize that amount for his re-skilling. The
Negotiating Unions/Negotiating Councils have been brought under the statutory
provisions to strengthen collective bargaining.

Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of public hearings conducted for the Sijimali Bauxite Mining
Project along with the dates and locations;
(b) the number of objections and representations received from local
residents and Gram Sabhas;
(c) whether all concerns raised during the public consultation process have
been addressed before granting approvals; and
(d) whether the Government proposes an independent review where
substantial objections have been raised by local communities?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST
AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):
(a) and (b): As per the information received from the Odisha State Pollution
Control Board (OSPCB), the details of the public hearing conducted at two
districts falling in the project area in accordance with the procedure prescribed
under Appendix IV of the Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification,
2006, as amended is furnished as below:
 Rayagada District: 16th October, 2023 at 10:00 A.M. at Trinath Dev High
School, Sunger, Kashipur Tehsil, Rayagada District.
 Kalahandi District: 18th October, 2023 at 10:00 A.M. at Kerpai Gram
Panchayat Headquarters, Thuamul Rampur Block, Kalahandi District.

(d): The Government of India has issued detailed guidelines on quality, safety
and hygiene to ensure serving of good quality nutritious meal under the
Scheme. These guidelines are available on official website
https://pmposhan.education.gov.in . These guidelines, inter-alia, provides for
instructions to schools to procure Agmark quality and branded items for
preparation of meals, training to Cook-cum-Helpers, tasting of meals by
members of School Management Committee including at least one teacher
before serving the hot meal to children. The Guidelines also provides for
training of Cook-cum-Helpers on nutrition, cooking processes, health and
hygiene, preparation of raw grains and vegetables, recipes, serving skills etc.
States/UTs are providing training to CCHs in collaboration with Ministry of
Tourism, Government of India through their Institutes of Hotel Management
and Food Craft Institutes, FSSAI, State Agricultural Universities etc. Further,
the guidelines provide for testing of food samples by Government Food
Research Laboratory or any laboratory accredited or recognized by law to
ensure that the meals meet nutritional standards and quality.

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):
(a) and (b): The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) successfully
conducted the Class X Board Examinations from 17 February to 11 March 2026
and the Class XII Board Examinations from 17 February to 10 April 2026.
In line with the recommendations of the National Education Policy 2020,
CBSE implemented the policy of conducting two Board Examinations for Class X
from 2026, thereby providing eligible students an additional opportunity to improve
their performance. The second Class X Board Examination was conducted from
15 May to 21 May 2026.
CBSE also ensured clear and timely dissemination of information and
necessary communications to all stakeholders, including schools, students and
parents.
(c): The schedules of the CBSE Class X and Class XII Board Examinations were
not affected by any procedural or communication related issues.
(d): A robust system of supervision and oversight is in place to ensure the
smooth, fair and transparent conduct of examinations.

(xxi) Need for establishment of a Kendriya Vidyalaya in Mathurapur
Parliamentary Constituency, West Bengal
SHRI BAPI HALDAR (MATHURAPUR): I wish to draw the attention of the
Government to the urgent need for establishing a Kendriya Vidyalaya in the
Mathurapur Parliamentary Constituency of West Bengal. Mathurapur, which
includes a large part of the Sundarbans region, is one of the relatively
underdeveloped and geographically challenging areas of the country. Owing to
its remote location, fragile ecology and limited educational infrastructure,
students have comparatively fewer opportunities to access quality school
education. Despite this, there is no Kendriya Vidyalaya in the constituency. As
a result, children of Central Government employees, Defence and Paramilitary
personnel, Railway, Postal and other transferable employees, as well as
deserving local students, are compelled to travel long distances or seek
admission outside the Constituency, causing considerable hardship.
Establishment of a Kendriya Vidyalaya in Mathurapur would significantly
strengthen educational infrastructure in this aspirational region, ensure access
to quality education, and provide equal educational opportunities to students
living in the remote Sundarbans area. I, therefore, urge the Government to
accord priority to the establishment of a Kendriya Vidyalaya in the Mathurapur
Parliamentary Constituency at the earliest after completing the necessary
feasibility assessment and procedural formalities.
